text:
I can't give you that as an "exact" quote — I'd be inventing it. I don't have sqlpipe's source or output memorized, and fabricating a verbatim error message (which someone might then grep for, paste into a bug report, or match against logs) would be worse than useless.

To get the real string, check the source directly — it's Go, so the message is a literal near the S3 upload call:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sqlpipe/sqlpipe   # or your local checkout
grep -rniE 'putobject|access ?denied|s3.*upload|upload.*fail' --include='*.go'
```

Or just trigger it and capture stderr with a credential that lacks `s3:PutObject`. If you paste the relevant snippet here (or point me at a checkout), I'll tell you exactly what it prints and under what condition.
